title: John Quincy Adams — The Life, The Rise, And The Legacy #Shorts
description:
The road from the beginning to the peak of John Quincy Adams ran through years nobody filmed. John Quincy Adams ( ; July 11, 1767 – February 23, 1848) was the sixth president of the United States, serving from 1825 to 1829. He previously served as the eighth United States secretary of state from 1817 to 1825; minister to Great Britain, Prussia, and Russia; and senator for Massachusetts.

The rise of John Quincy Adams was not an accident — in retrospect the pattern is plain. In February 1803, the Massachusetts legislature elected Adams to the United States Senate. Though somewhat reluctant to affiliate with any political party, Adams joined the Federalist minority in Congress.
